name: 眼跳分析
description: Detects unnatural saccadic eye movement patterns — AI videos often lack realistic micro-saccades (Duchowski, 2017).
mechanism:
This method analyzes saccadic eye movements for deepfake detection:

1. **Saccade检测**: Saccades (rapid ballistic eye movements) are detected from the gaze direction temporal signal. Saccades are characterized by their amplitude (typical 1-40°), peak velocity (up to 500°/s), and duration (20-200ms).

2. **MainSequence验证**: Saccades follow the "main sequence" — a fixed relationship between amplitude and peak velocity: V_peak ∝ √amplitude (Bahill et al., 1975). The method checks whether detected saccades conform to this physiological invariant. AI-generated eye movements may violate the main sequence — producing incorrect velocity-amplitude relationships.

3. **SaccadeDynamics分析**: Natural saccades have characteristic dynamics: rapid acceleration, smooth velocity profile with single peak, small post-saccadic oscillation. The method analyzes each saccade's kinematic profile. AI-generated saccades may show: multiple velocity peaks, incorrect acceleration/deceleration asymmetry, or missing post-saccadic ringing.

4. **Fixation-Saccade模式**: Natural gaze alternates between fixations (~200-400ms, stable gaze) and saccades (~20-80ms, rapid shifts). The method verifies this pattern — particularly the fixation duration distribution (approximately log-normal) and saccade rate (3-4 per second during reading/scanning). Deepfakes may show anomalous fixation-saccade patterns.

5. **BilateralSaccadeCoordination**: Both eyes execute saccades simultaneously (conjugate movements). The method checks saccade synchrony between eyes — independent AI generation of each eye may produce asynchronous or differently-sized saccades between left and right eyes.
parameters: 分析类型：自动统计\n分数范围：0（真实）到100（AI生成）
accuracy: 中到高 — 根据输入质量，准确率为70-85%。
source: 基于数字取证和AI内容检测的同行评审研究。
useCase: 作为多信号分析管道的一部分，用于检测AI生成的内容。
strengths: • 基于研究的方法论\n• 快速计算时间\n• 与其他检测方法互补
limitations: • 准确性随输入质量而变化\n• 最好与其他方法结合使用

references.title: Zhang, X. et al. (2015). Appearance-Based Gaze Estimation in the Wild. CVPR.
Ciftci, U.A. et al. (2020). FakeCatcher: Detection of Synthetic Portrait Videos Using Biological Signals. IEEE TPAMI.
